title: Equivariant marked nodal alteration over a trait
statement: A trait means the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring, a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. A complete strictly henselian trait has a maximal-ideal-adically complete henselian coordinate ring with separably closed residue field. Mixed characteristic means fraction-field characteristic zero and positive residue characteristic. Let $T$ be a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait and let $C$ be a normal integral flat projective $T$-scheme whose generic fibre is geometrically integral of positive dimension $d$. There are a finite dominant extension of traits $T_1\to T$, a finite group $G$, a marked split nodal tower $Y_d\to\cdots\to Y_0=T_1$ of length $d$, and a $G$-equivariant projective dominant generically finite morphism $q:Y_d\to C$ over $T$ (generically finite: finite over some dense open of $C$). The action on $C,T$ is trivial and the action on $T_1$ may be nontrivial. The tower and $q$ are equivariant, and $T_1$ is complete strictly henselian. There is a nonempty open $V\subset C$ such that $q^{-1}V\to V$ is a connected finite etale $G$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]; no semistability or regularity of the total $Y_i$ is asserted. A marked split nodal tower over a trait $T$ is a tower $Y_d\xrightarrow{f_d}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_1}Y_0=T$ of integral schemes, each $f_i$ projective and flat of finite presentation with geometrically connected reduced fibres of pure dimension one whose only singularities are ordinary double points (completed geometric local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$). Write $B_0=T_s$ for the closed point. Each $f_i$ has finitely many disjoint sections $\sigma_{ij}$ in its relative smooth locus; set $B_i=f_i^{-1}(B_{i-1})\cup\bigcup_j\sigma_{ij}(Y_{i-1})$ as a closed set. The map $f_i$ is smooth outside $B_{i-1}$. Split means that each fibre's irreducible components are geometrically irreducible and each of its nodes and its two branches are rational over the residue field of the base point. For a group action, the tower is equivariant, the unions of sections are stable, and the stabilizer of a base point acts trivially on the dual graph of its fibre. The dual graph has one vertex for each geometric irreducible component, one edge with its two ends for each node, and an attached marked leg for each section. Integral, regular, flat, finite type, finite, projective, and etale use [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-kun-projective], and [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Normal means all local rings are integrally closed domains. Quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over the base. Smoothness is as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and geometric integrality, reducedness, connectedness and irreducibility as in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].
